title: Intuitionistic interpolation from sequent proofs

based_on.title: Interpolation in extensions of first-order logic (arXiv:1807.11848v4)
based_on.pages: §1 pp.2–7; §3 pp.13–14, Definition 10, Lemma 11 and Theorem 12

summary: Extract a native intuitionistic interpolant and two cut-free factor trees, reversing the split at implication and negation when required.
abstract: An intuitionistic argument can use assumptions whose atom names do not occur in its conclusion. We construct a middle formula that carries just the information shared by the two parts of the argument. A recursion on the supplied sequent proof returns that formula together with two intuitionistic proof trees. Implication and negation require a reversed split in their antecedent premises, while disjunction combines the two branches according to the side that owns its assumption. We prove the common-atom bound throughout the construction, connect it to ordinary intuitionistic deduction, and follow concrete and atom-free examples.
